lib/controller-boot.ts.reason: Boot reconciliation now projects its abandons onto run_history, closing a live acceptance blocker: on the UAT instance 7 of 8 run_history rows claiming 'running' were zombies up to two days old, every one of them ALREADY carrying a run.abandoned spine event. Root cause is that both abandon emitters INSERT into spine_events directly (they need the spine_run_abandoned_cause_unique named-constraint idempotency a raw INSERT gives them) while run_history is written ONLY from inside emitSpineEvent, so the event log terminalised and the durable projection did not. A stuck row is not cosmetic: getActiveRun reads it, so the connection is refused every new run with 409 active_run_exists and its coverage checkpoint never leaves not_staged/not_committed (the RECORDS_NO_PROOF class). The +1 mass is repairTerminalRunHistoryDriftSqlite's terminalStatusForEventType branch set, which maps each of the five canonical terminal event types onto the status stores/run-history-writer.ts's toTerminalStatus would have derived, so a repaired row is indistinguishable from a writer-finalized one. That mapping is the load-bearing part: collapsing it to a single 'failed' would misreport a completed or cancelled run's outcome. Repair is deliberately fact-based, not time-based -- it reads the durable terminal event rather than a heartbeat/lease staleness threshold, which would need a guessed window and can be wrong in both directions (killing a slow live run, or waiting out the window before freeing a provably dead one). server/heartbeat-lease.ts was considered and rejected as the wrong primitive twice over: it is presentation-only and answers device-collector liveness, not run terminality. records_emitted is deliberately never written on either path, so records validly committed before the controller died stay committed per the RI-owner ruling. Proven by test/boot-orphan-run-history-projection.test.ts (4 tests): orphan terminalised with a typed reason, committed records retained, drift against an already-terminal spine repaired -- all three fail on the unmodified base -- plus a counterweight proving a run owned by the CURRENT incarnation is left running, which passes before and after and pins the no-over-correction half.

lib/postgres-spine.ts.reason: mergeEventRows fix for a silent data-loss bug (distinct rows sharing a null/duplicate event_seq collapsed onto the same dedup key). The explicit empty/backend branches and per-row fail-closed hydration are load-bearing backend parity, not incidental extraction candidates; the SQLite 50-to-200 slope and no-write oracle plus PostgreSQL authority cover them. This is the single seam every run kind (scheduled/manual/browser/cancelled) already funnels through; adding the hook here, rather than at each of the ~15 individual call sites across runtime/index.ts and runtime/scheduler.ts, is the whole point of the design (one seam, not N call-site edits). Proven load-bearing by test/run-history-writer-authority.test.ts (6 tests: started->finalized transition per run kind, idempotency under retried started/terminal events, terminal-only fallback insert).

server/connection-setup-plan.ts.reason: Deployment readiness measured from the manifest instead of a connector-name allowlist (2026-08-08, acceptance-contract D1). buildDeploymentReadiness previously decided provider-app readiness purely by membership in configuredProviderAuthConnectorKeys, an allowlist populated by two hardcoded per-provider adapters. The +4 mass is the manifest-declared branch: prefer the manifest's own deployment_config keys, test each against the observed environment (blank counts as absent), return ready only when none are missing, and otherwise name EXACTLY the missing subset rather than re-listing every declared key. The allowlist path is retained solely as the fallback for a manifest that declares no keys -- the one case this module has nothing to measure -- so the two existing per-provider adapters keep working unchanged. Each branch is a distinct load-bearing decision, not incidental structure; collapsing the missing-subset filter back into a blanket blocker list would restore the less precise message, and dropping the fallback would break the connectors whose readiness the adapters still own. Env is injected (deploymentEnv, defaulting to process.env) so the module stays a pure function of its inputs and a test can describe a deployment without mutating the process. Proven load-bearing by two discriminating console tests that fail on the unmodified base: readiness is measured from manifest-declared settings against the observed environment (absent/partial/blank/complete cases on a synthetic connector, no connector named in RI code), and a connector-key allowlist cannot declare readiness a deployment has not supplied.

server/connector-maintenance-sweep.ts.reason: P0/P1/P2 fleet evidence convergence correction (2026-07-30): periodic and startup bounded evidence maintenance must retain a keyset cursor through a durable cross-backend store, acquire a generation-and-token fenced lease before the full read/sweep/write unit, reject malformed/non-resumable results without overwriting the prior cursor, reject a malformed completed result that carries a cursor, retain progress on failure, and discard a completion when its lease was superseded. An incomplete NULL result is valid only when the leased current cursor is also NULL, because the bounded sweep uses the cursor-before-page to retry a heavy first-page fold; after a non-null cursor it remains fail-closed. Startup must likewise retry the valid first-page NULL only through its existing round cap. These independent scheduling-safety branches sit at the orchestration boundary; extracting them would conceal ownership/error ordering or split a small module into shallow helpers. SQLite/real-PostgreSQL restart, cursor-loss, heavy-first-page, overlap, and stale-writer regressions prove the paths.

server/connector-summary-read-model.ts.reason: Bounded evidence phase-progress fix (2026-07-30): a maintenance page must distinguish unbounded reconcile-then-fold from bounded existing-participant fold, cold missing-row creation, and generic canonical repair. Those phases share one cooperative absolute deadline: folding first is the proof that generic repairs cannot repeat a NULL-cursor first page without advancing its terminal checkpoint; no repair or fold batch starts after expiry; a started writer-fenced repair or finite event batch may finish; cold creation is capped to one small page of candidates. The aggregate receipt deliberately records the old/new minimum checkpoint, event count, participant count, repair duration, and explicit zero-progress state without per-connection data or an invented per-phase timeout. Collapsing the branches would conflate cold and existing evidence or either reintroduce starvation or hide deadline progress. Exact 25-row/274-event and 1ms/2,001-event SQLite plus real disposable-PostgreSQL mutation regressions prove phase order, finite work, unrelated-page isolation, restart/resume, and receipt invariants.

server/connector-summary-reconcile-obser.reason: Bounded evidence phase-progress fix (2026-07-30): the reconcile receipt serializes aggregate terminal-fold progress dimensions independently, preserving null for no participant/checkpoint while clamping numeric fields and retaining the existing allowlisted, payload-free telemetry boundary. server/records.ts.reason: TypeScript migration closure (2026-07-28): server/records.ts strict-plus type fixes add 7 conditional branches for null/undefined guards (string|null|undefined -> string narrowing), DevicePreparePlanEntry/DeviceRecordPlanEntry alignment, and exactOptionalPropertyTypes spreads. Shared ingest throughput fix (2026-08-06): ingestRecords holds one connector-instance ownership capability across the bounded request while preserving the existing ordered per-record durable/index phase, per-record failure isolation, and dual-backend dispatch. The added loop and outcome guards are the minimum control flow for those invariants and are proven by the focused two-stream fault oracle; removing them would either reacquire the bottleneck per record or collapse a failed record into a batch-wide rollback. Follow-up ordering correction (2026-08-06): the generic afterRecord completion callback is awaited between each record's storage phase and the next record, so acquisition provenance cannot be moved after the batch; its explicit error boundary and ordered callback path are proven by the route-level event-order oracle. Batch liveness correction (2026-08-07): ingestRecords keeps one authoritative connector-instance fence and schedules ordered derived-index work on a separate per-instance lane behind a release barrier, preserving batch lock reuse while allowing blob writers to proceed during embedding/index waits. The lane, per-record derived-error isolation, and release-barrier ordering are proven by the SQLite blob-route and lock-count oracles; removing them either restores blob starvation or lets newer derived work overtake older durable batches. Run-admission fence (2026-08-07, harden-ingest-run-admission-fence): PR #84 red-team found that a durable ingest write already admitted into the per-connector-instance write coordinator before owner-cancellation still committed after run_history recorded the run terminal -- runtime/index.ts's own cancellation is a client-side AbortSignal that cannot retroactively refuse a write the server already accepted. assertSqliteRunStillAdmitted checks run_history for (runId, connectorInstanceId) inside the same writeTransaction as the durable mutation it guards, so the check-then-write is atomic on SQLite's single writer connection; it fails CLOSED on a run_id with no matching row (spoofed/mistyped/foreign), not admitted, since a genuine run-bound write is always preceded by an awaited run.started spine insert. Opt-in via options.runId -- owner/API ingestion that never threads a run_id is unaffected. Checked once per record inside ingestRecordsWithinCoordinator's existing loop (not once per batch): the coordinator lock ingestRecords already holds for the whole batch does not serialize against the run's terminal write (a fully separate call path, runtime/index.ts's proc.on('close', ...) handler), and making the terminal writer share that lock was evaluated and rejected -- it would force cancellation to wait behind an unbounded in-flight batch, reintroducing the exact defect commit 73708a720 fixed and violating the sub-second terminalization contract runtime-cancel-run.test.ts/runtime-cancel-queue.test.ts already enforce. Measured cost: ~20.5us/record (~13% relative) on SQLite, a warmed 5-round 200-record benchmark. Proven by test/runtime-cancel-ingest-commit-boundary-probe.test.ts (9 tests): cancel-before-release refusal, release-before-cancel preservation, cross-connection run_id-collision spoof resistance, fail-closed on an unrecognized run_id, HTTP wire-through from the real POST /v1/ingest/:stream route, and Postgres parity for all of the above.

server/ref-control.ts.reason: Fable ruling terminal-read-architecture-fable-0730.md §8 (2026-07-30, identity_inventory) + design doc add-source-perf-design-agy-0730.md R4/R5 (2026-07-30, retained_count_summary). The second increment adds the retained_count_summary named profile to the same listConnectorSummaryPage/getConnectorSummaryForRoute projection (one-projection-N-profiles, not a third projection): projectConnectorRetainedCountSummaryPage's own bounded dependency read (identity page + one evidence-row batch + one acquisition-batch-store batch, zero spine/browser-surface/runtime/schedule/run-history reads), its extracted deriveRetainedCountState helper (kept separate specifically to hold the per-row closure under the cognitive-complexity budget), a third profile branch and overload at each public entry point, and the new getConnectorSummaryForRoute overload. Removing the branch would either fold the retained-count path into the full projection (defeating the cost reduction the profile exists to prove) or duplicate the two public functions a second time. PERSISTED known_zero READ-PROOF (2026-08-09, +5 measured, 215 -> 220): Ruling R2's converse prohibition. A `count_state` is derived once at repair time and then served verbatim out of stream_records_json; repair classification never inspects that column, so a row whose checkpoint and total have not moved is never revisited and a `known_zero` written before positive proof was required keeps reaching every consumer on a row reading a healthy `current`. Measured on the live UAT instance: 13 served streams asserted a proven exact zero, and not one had a record-source checkpoint entry -- five had no runtime fact whatsoever. The added mass is parseObservedCheckpointStreams (a defensive parse of the stored record checkpoint, yielding an empty observation set rather than a fabricated one on a malformed column) plus downgradePersistedCountState, which holds BOTH read-boundary invalidations in one named place: the pre-existing non-current-snapshot `stale` downgrade and the new coverage re-proof. The re-proof honours two independent proof channels and either suffices -- a record-side checkpoint entry (the write path's own canonical proof, load-bearing so an observed-then-emptied stream stays a true zero on a connection that never measured collection coverage) or run-side positive coverage evidence judged by @pdpp/reference-contract/evidence's evaluateStreamCoherence via persistedZeroRetainsCoverageProof. Requiring BOTH channels was measured to withdraw 10 genuinely proven zeros across the existing suites; requiring neither is the defect itself. The judgement is NOT reimplemented here -- it delegates to the same contract module connector-coverage-policy.ts already uses, so the RI cannot drift from conformance tooling. Collapsing the two invalidations into one predicate would lose the `stale`-vs-`unobserved` distinction (a carried-over count that was once real vs. no count claim at all), and inlining them at the call site would duplicate the judgement across the full projection and the retained_count_summary profile. NOTE: the committed baseline of 196 had drifted stale; the unmodified base measures 215 (confirmed via measure-mass.ts against this branch's HEAD with the change stashed), so 19 of the 24-point gap to the old ceiling predates this change and is not attributable to it. Proven load-bearing by connector-summary-persisted-count-state-read-proof.test.ts (3 tests: no-runtime-fact and open-checkpoint rows both fail on the unmodified base with actual 'known_zero' vs expected 'unobserved'; the proven-zero counterweight passes before AND after, pinning that true zeros are not over-corrected away). Collection-scope staleness wiring (2026-08-09): the final adversarial review found the staleness comparator had ZERO production callers -- proven correct in isolation, never consulted, so narrowing a scope did not declassify coverage committed under the old boundary. The added mass is the wiring that closes it: collectionEvidenceScopeIsStale (a pure two-fingerprint comparison), one declared-vs-measured comparison per REPORT (deliberately not per stream -- this must never become an N+1), the entry-level declassification branch that maps a stale match onto the honest `unknown` while leaving a manifest-declared accepted-absence axis untouched (that axis is a statement about the stream, not a measurement), and the read of the declared fingerprint off the SAME connector-state projection deriveLocalCoverageAxis is already built from, so binding coverage to the boundary costs no additional query on either backend. Each branch is a distinct honest outcome: collapsing the accepted-absence carve-out would declassify streams that owe no data, and hoisting the comparison per stream would multiply reads. Proven by test/collection-scope-staleness-projection.test.ts, which drives the REAL projection (not the comparator directly) with genuine `complete` baselines, and is mutation-proven: forcing evidenceScopeIsStale to false -- the exact defect the review found -- fails the narrow and clear cases.

server/routes/owner-connection-collectio.reason: New file (2026-08-09, owner-settable local collection scope). The independent audit rejected the prior lane because local-collection-scope.ts had ZERO production callers: nothing ever wrote $collection_scope, so every run was unscoped by construction and the proof machinery had no boundary to prove anything about. This is the write path that makes a bounded collection horizon reachable at all. The measured mass is validation and three route handlers, and each branch is a distinct honest outcome rather than incidental structure: parseScopeBody REJECTS rather than coerces (a `since` the server cannot parse would become a boundary that silently matches everything, and a non-string root would widen the owner's selection -- an owner who mistypes a bound must be told, not quietly given a full-corpus run that reports itself as scoped), which needs the since-absent / since-malformed / since-unparseable / roots-not-array / roots-entry-invalid / neither-declared cases separated because each is a different message the owner acts on differently. The three handlers (GET inspect, PUT declare, DELETE clear) share writeScope, which is where declassification lives: changing OR clearing the boundary drops prior coverage proof, because evidence measured against a different region does not describe the new one and must be recomputed by a fresh run rather than reinterpreted. Clearing is deliberately routed through the same path as any other change (it is a change to `unscoped`, not an absence of one), which is why DELETE is not a separate simpler branch. Persistence reuses connector_state under a reserved $-prefixed key rather than adding a column -- source_binding_json is hashed into the connection's identity so a scope edit there would be a re-identification, and the device_source_instances JSON columns are rewritten every heartbeat -- so this route needs no migration and no second transport: the same write both stores the boundary and delivers it on the state read the collector already performs at run start. Proven by test/local-collection-scope.test.ts (11 tests, including fingerprint-recomputed-on-read so a tampered row cannot assert a boundary its own bounds do not describe, malformed entries degrading to unscoped rather than a guessed bound, and evidence-vs-declared staleness in both directions) and by the collector-side contract suite that drives a real child process against a real server.

server/stores/run-history-writer.ts.reason: New file (2026-07-30, Authority Slice A / generalize-run-history-write-authority): the kind-neutral run_history writer hooked into emitSpineEvent. Each branch is load-bearing idempotency/identity-safety logic, not incidental structure; collapsing them would either silently duplicate a row under a race or write fabricated identity. Proven by test/run-history-writer-authority.test.ts (6 tests covering every branch: per-run-kind started->finalized transition, retried-started idempotency, retried-terminal idempotency, terminal-only fallback insert, scheduler-merge-not-duplicate, scheduler_managed reader scoping). REVISE (second gate pass, 2026-07-30, G1 closure): +6 mass for the new run.progress_reported branch on both backends (collectionRateMergeJson's undefined-guard against writing an empty merge on a progress event carrying no rate change, plus the SQLite/Postgres branch dispatch itself) that atomically merges collection_rate into a still-running row's facts_json, fenced by status='running' so a concurrent/later terminal write always wins. This closes a live G1 violation the gate reproduced against the sanctioned Postgres instance (a spine_events read fired on every connector-summary route for a currently-running connection); the branch is the load-bearing fence, not incidental structure. Proven by test/active-run-summary-zero-spine.test.ts (6 tests, dual-backend, zero skips): the merge lands correctly, a stale post-terminal progress event is a no-op, and zero spine_events statements survive for in-progress/terminal/no-run GETs on both SQLite and real Postgres. EMPTY-TERMINAL-ERROR FIX (2026-08-08, +6 mass): a live run (run_1786242751717) stored terminal_reason=connector_protocol_violation with connector_error_json NULL -- the owner saw a terminal failure carrying no explanation at all, while the runtime's precise reason reached only the container log. Root cause: connectorErrorJsonFromTerminalData reassembled the error strictly from the executor's flattened connector_error_* fields, and a run the RUNTIME failed carries none of them (the connector reported DONE with no error of its own), so the function returned null. The added branch is the runtime-authored fallback: when no connector_error_* field is present, persist the terminal event's own failure_message (the runtime-authored explanation buildTerminalErrorFields already puts on the spine event) tagged with its failure_origin, so any genuine terminal failure carries a typed reason visible to the owner. It is deliberately a FALLBACK, not a merge -- a connector-reported DONE.error remains authoritative and is written verbatim, because the connector's own explanation is more specific than the runtime's generic line. The mass is the presence-test for the three connector_error_* fields plus the typed-string guard on failure_message; collapsing them would either overwrite a connector-authored error with a vaguer runtime line or write a fabricated non-string message. Proven load-bearing by two discriminating tests in test/run-history-writer-authority.test.ts: a runtime-authored terminal failure stores its failure_message as the connector error (fails on the unmodified base), and a connector-reported terminal error is preserved verbatim over the runtime fallback (passes both before and after, pinning the no-overwrite half).
